question: Which compound from the following is an unsaturated hydrocarbon?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ethene**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hydrocarbons** are organic compounds consisting entirely of **Hydrogen** and **Carbon** atoms. They are classified into two main categories: **saturated** and **unsaturated** based on the types of bonds present between the carbon atoms.
 
• **Unsaturated hydrocarbons** are those hydrocarbons that contain at least one **double bond** or **triple bond** between adjacent carbon atoms. These compounds are more reactive than saturated ones.
 
• **Ethene** (C2H4), also known as **ethylene**, belongs to the **alkene** group. It contains a **carbon-carbon double bond** (C=C), which makes it an **unsaturated hydrocarbon**. ***Hence, option 1 is the correct answer.***
 
• **Methane** (CH4) is the simplest **alkane**. It consists of a single carbon atom bonded to four hydrogen atoms through **single covalent bonds**, making it a **saturated hydrocarbon**. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Propane** (C3H8) and **Butane** (C4H10) are also members of the **alkane** series. They consist of carbon chains where all carbon-carbon bonds are **single bonds**. These are classified as **saturated hydrocarbons**. ***Hence, options 2 and 4 are incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Alkanes (Saturated Hydrocarbons):**
 
 
• The general formula for **alkanes** is **CnH2n+2**.
 
• In these molecules, every **carbon atom** is **sp3 hybridized**, forming four sigma bonds.
 
• Common examples include **Ethane**, **Pentane**, and **Hexane**. They are generally used as **fuels** due to their high **combustion** energy.
 
 
 
• **Alkenes and Alkynes (Unsaturated Hydrocarbons):**
 
 
• **Alkenes** contain at least one **double bond** and follow the general formula **CnH2n**. Carbon atoms in the double bond are **sp2 hybridized**.
 
• **Alkynes** contain at least one **triple bond** and follow the general formula **CnH2n-2** (e.g., **Ethyne** or Acetylene). Carbon atoms in the triple bond are **sp hybridized**.
 
• Unsaturated hydrocarbons undergo **addition reactions** (like **hydrogenation** or **bromination**) to become saturated.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Tests:**
 
 
• The **Bromine Water Test** is used to distinguish between saturated and unsaturated compounds. An **unsaturated hydrocarbon** will decolorize the **reddish-brown bromine water**, while a saturated one will not react under normal conditions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Methane** is the primary component of **Natural Gas** and **Biogas**. It is a potent **greenhouse gas** but is widely used as a clean-burning **fuel**.
 
• **Propane** and **Butane** are the main constituents of **Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG)**, which is used globally for **cooking** and **heating**.
 
• **Ethene** plays a vital biological role as a **plant hormone** responsible for the **ripening of fruits**. Industrially, it is the precursor for **polyethylene (polythene)**, the most common **plastic** in use today.
 
• The number of carbon atoms determines the prefix of the name: **Meth-** (1), **Eth-** (2), **Prop-** (3), **But-** (4), **Pent-** (5), etc.
